answer: Dormancy-Weighted Task Auctions.** Each identity earns task rights only by completing unpredictable, time-boxed micro-tasks that require sustained attention; agents must wander across shifting task queues to maintain eligibility. Rights decay if skipped. An attacker cloning identities pays the full compute and latency cost per clone while rewards split across a fixed pool, so each marginal clone subtracts value. Like splitting timber, the cost grows faster than the yield. A cloned swarm also loses the coordination quality a single sonnet of steady work sustains,
